title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Senior Backend Engineer
About us
We're creating the foundational backend systems that power private market access, from secure authentication and transaction processing to portfolio management and regulatory compliance.
The Role
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to own the systems where money moves and balances have to be correct - the ledger, transaction processing, and the settlement and reconciliation workflows behind our platform. This is the correctness core of what we build. If a balance is wrong, a transaction double-processes, or a reconciliation silently drifts, nothing else we build matters.
You'll design the double-entry ledger, the money-movement engine, and the long-running state machines that carry complex financial workflows to completion reliably over hours, days, or weeks. You'll reason about idempotency, concurrency, partial failure, and replay as a matter of habit, not as an afterthought.
You'll own core infrastructure decisions and set the standard for how we build financial systems.
Requirements
What You'll Do

• Design and build the double-entry ledger and money-movement engine that all transactions reconcile against

• Model complex financial workflows as robust, observable state machines that run reliably over long periods

• Guarantee financial correctness under concurrency: idempotent operations, transactional integrity, and reconciliation that ties out to the cent

• Handle partial-failure and replay cases so no event is lost, duplicated, or applied twice

• Build secure, well-versioned APIs

• Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and data models

• Debug production issues and own the reliability of mission-critical financial workflows

What We're Looking For

• 5+ years of backend development on production systems

• Demonstrated money-movement correctness experience: you've built a ledger, settlement system, payments core, or transaction-processing system and can talk in detail about how you kept it correct

• Concurrency and idempotency depth: you can explain, from experience, how you handled double-processing, race conditions on balances, and replay

• Reconciliation experience: you've built or owned systems that had to tie out exactly, and you know what happens when they don't

• Strong TDD practices: you write tests first and maintain comprehensive coverage

• Domain-Driven Design expertise: you model complex financial domains accurately

• Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: schema design, transactions, isolation levels, optimization

• Strong in a modern backend stack: we work in TypeScript/Node.js, Go and on the JVM ecosystem; we value real depth in either and the range to pick up the other

• Cloud deployment experience

• Startup mentality: comfortable with ambiguity, high autonomy, driving solutions without detailed specs

Nice to Have

• Payments, banking, brokerage, or investment-platform systems experience

• Securities, custody, or portfolio/NAV domain knowledge

• Event-driven architectures and message queues

• Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation)

• Understanding of KYC/AML or compliance frameworks

• Accounting principles or financial modeling

In this landscape, ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) stand out as particularly compelling devices: fully compatible with standard CMOS fabrication processes, non-volatile, reconfigurable, and capable of storing intermediate polarization states - a property that naturally enables ternary logic within a single device. ABOUT THE TEAM:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware-and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

- Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

- Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

- Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

- Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

- Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

- Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

- Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

- Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

- Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

- Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

- Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

- Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

title: Senior Linux Application Engineer (all genders) – Python & IoT Edge
description:

As Senior Linux Application Engineer (all genders) in our IoT team, you build the software foundation for all our Linux-based devices, on ARM and x86. At its core is a platform layer that unifies shared components such as health monitoring and logging. Every device type then works the same way, and product features build on one solid base.

The role combines architecture and hands-on engineering: clean, object-oriented software, plus ownership of how it is built, deployed, updated and monitored across the fleet. Your code sits close to the hardware but runs on top of Linux.

Kernel development and microcontroller firmware are not part of the job. If well-designed software for Linux devices is your thing, you’ll feel at home here.

As we are looking for a hands-on developer, a live coding session is an integral part of our interview process.

What to expect

- Unified platform layer: Design and build a platform layer that covers all our device types, both ARM and x86. It provides shared components such as health monitoring, logging, configuration, OTA updates and hardware abstraction.

- Software architecture: Define clear interfaces between the platform and the applications on top of it. Consolidate the codebase so that new device types and components plug in easily.

- Application development: Build Python services on top of the platform, inside our dockerized main application.

- Device integration: Connect peripherals such as modems, watchdogs, cameras and AI accelerators through existing drivers, SDKs and Linux interfaces, behind a clean hardware abstraction.

- Reliability and observability: Make our fleet secure, resilient and transparent through OTA updates, networking, inter-process communication and fleet-wide monitoring of device health.

- Debugging: Analyze and solve complex issues at application and system level, such as memory leaks, network instability or service failures.

- Ownership and mentoring: Take end-to-end responsibility, guide other engineers technically, and raise our engineering standards.

Inspire us by

- Senior software engineering experience: 5+ years of professional software development, with a strong part of it on Linux-based devices or edge systems.

- Strong OOP skills: Deep experience with object-oriented design in (preferably) Python. Experience in another OOP language such as C++, Java or Rust is a plus.

- Architecture know-how: You have designed and evolved software architectures, applied design patterns, and made trade-off decisions you can explain clearly. Ideally you have built a platform, framework or shared library that other teams or services build on.

- IoT background: Hands-on experience building software for connected devices, ideally operated as a fleet in the field.

- Linux user-space expertise: Solid knowledge of Linux, systemd, networking, IPC, Bash and Docker, ideally across different hardware architectures (ARM and x86).

- Debugging skills: Experience troubleshooting system-level issues with tools such as GDB, tcpdump, Valgrind or profilers.

- Engineering mindset: Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Language skills: Fluent English (C1).

STRONG PLUS

- Experience building, customizing and maintaining Linux images with Yocto.

- Experience operating large-scale IoT fleets, including OTA updates and device monitoring

- Familiarity with MQTT and Protocol Buffers (ProtoBuf)

- Knowledge of industrial hardware, cameras, AI accelerators, modems or network devices

- Experience with edge AI, computer vision or machine learning

Our team works across custom silicon, embedded systems, operating systems, and cloud services to build reliable consumer devices and the platforms behind them. We connect kernel development with the broader software stack to deliver complete product capabilities.

As an Operating Systems Engineer focused on the Linux kernel, you will design, develop, and maintain the kernel capabilities that underpin OpenAI’s consumer devices. You’ll bring deep expertise in one or more Linux kernel subsystems and carry solutions through the higher-level software stack.

Your ownership will extend into the userspace services, libraries, tools, and interfaces needed to deliver complete product features. You’ll shape the boundaries between kernel and userspace, make design decisions across the stack, and see your work through development, integration, and production.
